Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

and the backup folder", "output": "We are maintaining the family photo importer that brings pictures from phones and memory cards into the shared archive, and this is my update for the next work session. The importer is used by my sister Leah, my uncle Peter, and me, and none of us is comfortable losing the original files. So the request is to make the next version easier to check without changing the way the family names its albums. The old laptop is still running the current copy, and the replacement laptop has a test library with photographs from our own trips.

The importer should read the date taken field when it exists and use the date the file was copied only when the camera date is missing. Last Saturday, Peter tried twelve pictures from a small camera, and four had no date taken value. The other eight went into the April Coast Walk album with their camera dates. The four without dates went into an album called Undated Review rather than being mixed into the current month. Please keep that distinction visible in the log, and do not treat an empty date as proof that a picture was taken today.

The most important setting is archive.retain_originals and it must remain enabled while the importer makes smaller display copies for the family website. The original camera files should stay untouched in the incoming folder until a person checks the import. The setting is used on the test laptop as well as the old laptop, and the family wants the same value on both machines. The scan should report if the setting is absent, but nobody has asked for the importer to delete or repair a setting automatically. The original filename should also remain visible beside any shorter display name so Leah can compare the two.

Duplicates are another concern because Peter sometimes copies a card twice before he has sorted the first batch. The importer currently flags files with the same size and matching image contents, but it should not decide that two photographs are duplicates only because they were taken on the same day in the same place. A burst of six pictures of the pier can look almost alike and still show different waves. The family wants a review row for a likely duplicate with both filenames and both dates shown side by side. Do not remove either file during that review. The person doing the import will choose what to keep.

Checks for the next test
1. Confirm that an import of twenty-seven files reports twenty-seven scanned files, even if three are placed in Undated Review. The scanned count is the number of files read from the card, and the review count is a separate number.
2. Use a card with two copies of the same beach image and one similar but different image. The exact copy should be flagged for review, and the similar image should remain a separate entry.
3. Check the display copy by opening it on a phone and make sure it is small enough to load on the family website while the original remains full size in the incoming folder.
4. Unplug the card after the scan has finished and confirm the log still shows the source card name and the album chosen by the person doing the import.

These are checks for the test session, not claims that the current build already passes them.

On the old laptop, the family folder has seven named albums, and the test library has two extra albums that are only for test photographs. Please do not copy those two test album names into the family library by default. Leah asked that the album picker show the newest album at the top because she adds an album before each trip. Peter wants the existing album names to stay exactly as they are since he has printed labels for three storage boxes. We can test the order with a temporary album called Winter Harbor, but we should remove that temporary test album after the ordering check is complete.

Leah said, “I can review the undated pictures on Sunday, but please leave them together so I can tell what came from the same card.” That is why the Undated Review album should keep the original card grouping in its details. If the importer cannot keep that grouping, it should mark the group information as unavailable rather than inventing a card order. The import screen can still show the filenames in their original order, and the log should record when that order came from the card. The family has not decided whether the website should show any undated picture, and that question is not part of this maintenance request.

There is one condition for the backup check: if the external drive is not connected, the importer may finish reading the card, but it must show that the backup has not been made and wait before telling the person the import is complete. When the drive is connected, the test should copy the untouched originals into the dated backup folder and report the folder name. The backup drive currently has about two hundred gigabytes free, and the test library uses about nine gigabytes, so there is room for this session. But do not use those figures as a promise about future capacity. If a file cannot be copied, keep its import entry visible and show the filename that needs attention.

For the session notes, record which laptop was used, the card name, the number of files read, the number sent to Undated Review, and whether the backup drive was connected. Use the local time shown by the laptop and do not convert it to another time zone. Peter asked that the notes fit on one printed page, but the file list can be attached separately if it is too long. The printed page should include the date of the test and the importer version so we can tell this run apart from the earlier practice run. Those notes are for comparing tests and are not a sign-off.

At the end of the session, we need to know whether the date handling, the duplicate review, and the backup condition behaved as requested. If anything differs, write down what happened and which filename or album was involved. Do not quietly rename the originals to make the report look tidy. The family will look over the notes together before choosing any follow-up work, and the next import should still be treated as a test until we have checked the files on both laptops and confirmed that the originals are present in the incoming folder and the backup folder."}]
